doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Joining the Messengers and moving to New York
title: Leaving Chicago in 1956: Max Roach at the Beehive
summary: Side 2 begins; Ware recounts the Messengers visiting Chicago and Leo Blevins taking him to meet Max Roach and Clifford Brown at the Beehive.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Would you talk a little bit about the time immediately preceeding your departure from Chicago to New York?
Well, that was '56. The Jazz Messengers

had been in town -- I didn't catch the first, the original, group -- that was the one with Horace Mobley Donald and Hank Moby, Don Byrd, Doug Watkins, and Art Blakey Reckie -- That's the original Messengers they were the originals. They had been in, and I missed the band, and Max was working at the Beehive, and I had met Max before --back in the forties -- when he was with Bird Byrd, so Little Leo Blevins got me one night -- late one night, and said, "C'mon, Willie, let's go out and catch Max. -- -- " play some nights."

I had heard about Clifford Brown, had never met him -- and Malachi told me they were in the band down at Morris Brown College -- and Clifford had his first automobile accident in that college band, and spoke about it. I had heard what a great trumpet player he was, and I had hardly heard the band -- I didn't have access to no records, or recordings of the Max Roach Quintet: Clifford and Harold Land and Richie Powell and George Morrow. So I said, "Okay Leo" -- Leo wanted to get over to the club and all that ... and so I went with him, and we went by the Beehive, and I guess we got there just before the last set, and the crowd was kind of thinned out and Max was off the stand, and Leo introduced me to him, and Brownie.

Yeah, Leo -- see, he was on top of everybody. Like Dexter used to stay at his house, and the late Rahsaan Roland Kirk used to stay at his house also. Well, Leo was like that -- he was the type of cat who played with
quite a few of them, and was always ready for a jam session. He was a go-getter.
